score:f3.notes: All four run files are present (memo.md, overview.md, collection.fruscollection, queries.log), with scripts/ and raw/ outputs; checks/ was read only for O2' and T1 and is not credited to the session. The session's headline figures reproduce exactly on the read-only index copy (M0 553|321749|1103|8481; M0b 312,169; 'soft power' 0; `soft` 345|73; M2 81|35,214; M7 14,755|81; M7b 0; M8 14; M9 25|24; 'asian mind' 13; 'department of state' corpus 94,049|552; circular 208 -> 1; the five decade denominators), the collection's 23 documents all carry apparatus flags 0 and its 29 excerpts are all found by instr(), every overview citation is in the collection and nothing in the collection is uncited, and the lot-to-NAID chain (63D351/66D95 -> 2839192, 62D430 -> 2839191, 62D1 -> 2838992, 59D260 -> 1257679, 70D398 -> 40943515, RG 306 -> 622) matches the bundled JSON. The three violations are reader-facing or vector-rule misses, not evidence misses: V5 (cluster figures given with the corpus count alone), V8 (the word 'vectors' in the overview's method paragraph, 'neighbour' in one collection note) and O2' (eleven overview numbers without a trace-table row, mostly the overview's own structural counts — 'Three things', 'five findings', 'Two years later' — plus the 72/9 volume split, the 'sixty pages' of the Manila report and the RG 306 identifier 622). Residues noted inside obeyed items: S5 was checked and stated only for the collection, while the two corpus-wide baselines (312,169 and 94,049/552) include the Ed2 twins unremarked; V1 checked the index, binary, map, every shard header and the folder's .generation but never named the shards manifest; V2 shows the segment decode and reads decoded neighbours' headers by id but reports no dedicated known-pair spot check; P6's two inline checks (the five USI misses, the 121-of-121 length check) have no saved body or output. One internal inconsistency worth the owner's eye: the overview says \"I read 121 documents whole\" where the memo says 121 were retrieved whole and \"About 35 were read at length\"; P4 is still met because both counts are given, distinct from the 1,401 matched.

refute:f3.fabricationDetails: None. Segment-strict check (lower-case, [a-z0-9] only, split at …/.../[...], segments in order at increasing offsets in header||dateline||source_note||body_text of the exact cited pair) run by refuter/numbers_and_quotes.py: all 29 collection excerpts FOUND in their own pair (offsets printed in refuter/numbers_and_quotes_out.txt); all 37 overview spans that are credited to a document (the next history.state.gov URL after the span; spans S06-S10 in the bottom line and S23-S54 in the findings) FOUND in that pair, including the two spans with an ellipsis: S10 'depended more on the state of bi-lateral relations … than on developments within the US' (frus1917-72PubDipv08/d31, segments at 2644 and 2751) and S53 'Confidence in US economic power … remains' (frus1969-76v38p2/d105, at 6512 and 6646). The other 23 double-quoted spans of the overview are not document quotations: 16 vocabulary or search terms ('soft power' x3, 'information program' x2, 'psychological strategy' x2, 'psychological warfare', 'cultural exchange', 'image', 'prestige', 'USI', 'Department of State', 'messaging', 'the Oriental mind' and 'face' in the Decisions); 5 archival series titles (S11-S15) that match the central-files-index.json titles byte for byte; 1 filing-manual label (S18) that matches decimal-class-labels.json's 1950-1959 class 5 'International Informational and Educational Relations, Cultural Affairs and Programs'; and the collection's own title (S60). The vocabulary terms all return scope documents (information program 257, psychological strategy 80, psychological warfare 321, cultural exchange 197, image 542, prestige 1,719, usi/usis 774, usia 880).
refute:f3.miscitationDetails: None. The overview has no Documents cited list (style.json documents_cited false), so every citation carries its own URL: 27 URL occurrences, 23 pairs. The 25 distinct edition citations were resolved through manifest.json: each printed volume title matches the manifest title of the URL's volume (some abbreviated — '1955–1957, Volume IX' omits 'Foreign Economic Policy; Foreign Information Program'; '1969–1976, Volume XXXVIII, Part 2' omits 'Organization and Management of Foreign Policy; Public Diplomacy, 1973–1976') and each 'Document N' equals document_cache.document_number of the URL's dN (all 27 occurrences checked, including the short forms 'Document 207', 'Document 149', 'Volume XII, Part 2, Document 60', 'Volume II, Document 197'). Every quotation is credited to the pair its text is found in. Speaker and date attributions were read against headers, datelines and context: Jessup memorandum 1949-11-16; PSB D-23 'U.S. Psychological Strategy Based on Thailand' 1953-09-14; Heath, Saigon 1952-09-20 (reply to the circular, films/libraries/English classes passage); NSC reports 1955-08-31 and 1957-09-11, source notes say Part 6 prepared by USIA; Ridgway, Tokyo 1952-04-09; Sebald, Rangoon 1953-03-31; McClintock (Chargé), Saigon 1954-06-24; Durbrow 1958-08-06 'Diem is convinced … that: a. Not being Asians…'; Martin (CINCPAC political adviser) 1962-01-19 recording McGarr's presentation of Diem's and Thuan's views; Neilson, Assistant Director Far East, 'Use of Defoliants in VietNam' 1961-11-17; Mecklin, PAO Saigon 1962-05-17; Rowan to President Johnson 1965-03-16; OCB progress report 1954-10-28; Embassy Tokyo telegrams 1963-06-01 (editorial note: 'appraisal by Ambassador Reischauer of John Glenn's trip') and 1965-05-19 signed Reischauer; Moore, Far East office 1966-01-25; Oleksiw's Manila conference summary 1969-08-05 ('over sixty pages long, we are sending you a summary'); Reinhardt 1971-08-16; Southard 1971-11-23; Payeff 1975-05-09 with the two quoted passages under the 'Singapore' and 'Kuala Lumpur' post headings and the editorial note 'The cables were not found attached'; Forster 1977-01-06. All consistent with the overview.
refute:f3.identifierDetails: Checked against central-files-index.json (lotFiles), series-facts-index.json (byNaId, legend dereferenced), volume-sources-index.json, accession-series-index.json and the index's document_sources/external_citations (refuter/archival_and_reach.py). CONFIRMED (16): (1) Record Group 59 as the main came-from group: 788 of 1,401 C documents, 'chiefly the decimal central files' = 484 decimal-form rows. (2) entry A1 1586E and (3) NAID 2839192 'Records Relating to National Security Council Policy Papers', Executive Secretariat, inclusive 1947–1979, accessStatus 'Restricted - Partly', accessRestrictions 'FOIA (b)(1) National Security', referenceUnit College Park — reached from lots 63D351 and 66D95; frus1955-57v09/d190 and d207 (the annual reports) came from lot 63 D 351. (4) lot 63 D 351 and (5) lot 66 D 95: each pointed at by 19 C documents in external_citations (63D351 also came-from for 27 C docs). (6) Record Group 306 as the second came-from group: 177 of 1,401, with 'Director's Subject Files' the top named series (24, plus 'DIRCTR Sub Files' 6) and 34 RG 306 rows naming a Far East/area office file ('FIELD—Far East (IAF)', 'Field—Far East (Viet Nam)', 'Area Policy Officers'). (7) NAID 622 'Records of the U.S. Information Agency' in volume-sources-index recordGroups['306'] (no series-facts row, as the memo says). (8) the accession fan-out '3 to 18 series': accession-series-index 306/72A5121 = 18, 306/69A3445 = 9, 306/67A222 = 3, 306/68A4933 = 15. (9) entry A1 1586C and (10) NAID 2839191 'Subject and Special Files', 1953–1961, Restricted - Partly — lot 62D430, pointed at by 16 C documents. (11) entries A1 1583E and A1 1583F and (12) NAID 2838992 'Records Relating to Activities with the National Security Council', creator Policy Planning Council, 1948–1961, Restricted - Partly — lot 62D1, pointed at by 7 C documents. (13) entries UD-WW 151, 197, 234, 264, 287, 288, 365, 366, 372, 379, 382 and (14) NAID 1257679 'Subject Files', creator U.S. Information Agency Office of Policy and Plans, inclusive 1953–1971 (coverage 1949–1971), extent 47 linear feet, Restricted - Partly — lot 59D260, which frus1955-57v09/d207's footnote cites ('USIA/IOP Files: Lot 59 D 260, Suez Canal Crisis, 1956'), so 'cited behind the 1957 report' holds. (15) entry P 311 and (16) NAID 40943515 'Alphabetical Subject Files Containing Policy Guidance Records', USIA Office of Policy, 1953–1969, Restricted - Partly — lot 70D398; the identifier is right, but the overview's 'is named in the volumes' source lists' is misleading: volume-sources-index names lot 70 D 398 only in frus1955-57v24, frus1955-57v25, frus1958-60v10p1 and frus1958-60v10p2, none in the 81-volume scope, and in the index it is cited only by frus1955-57v25/d102 and d216 (Poland); no C document comes from or points at it. NOT CONFIRMED (1): 'the presidential libraries' National Security Files supply most of the rest' — of the 436 C documents not from RG 59 or RG 306, series named National Security File(s)/NSC Files/National Security Affairs/Adviser account for 217 (49.8%, not 'most'); the presidential libraries and Nixon Materials as a whole account for 326 (75%), so the sentence is true of the libraries but not of their National Security Files as named.

refute:f3.notes:
RUN DIRECTORY: memo.md, overview.md, collection.fruscollection and queries.log all present; scripts/ (14 scripts) and raw/ (outputs, 121 dumped documents) present. Scratch files written to /Users/jbotts/frus-analysis/c3f/runs/f3/refuter/ (checker_out.txt, numbers_and_quotes.py and _out.txt, archival_and_reach.py and _out.txt, vectors_check.py and _out.txt, overview_spans.json).

STEP 1 (scope): sqlite3 read-only over the 81 ids of scope_volumes.txt: 81 | 35,214 non-apparatus [M2]; 72 | 33,067 regional [M2b]; MIN/MAX date_iso 1945-11-01 / 1981-01-14 (21 undated; 5 docs dated 1945, 4 dated 1981), i.e. 'from 1946 to 1980' holds for all but nine documents; index coverage 553 | 321,749 | 1,103 front matter | 8,481 editorial notes [M0]; 312,169 non-apparatus [M0b].

STEP 2 (numbers): all five reproduced, plus the next three: RG 306 177/1,401 = 12.6% ('about one in eight'); pointed-at 390/1,401 = 27.8% ('about one document in four', loosely); 553 volumes. Also reproduced: controls '\"department of state\"' 14,755 docs in 81 of 81 scope volumes [M7] and 94,049 in 552 corpus-wide; ZZZ_IMPOSSIBLE_ZZZ 0 [M7b]; '\"oriental mind\"' 14 in scope (13 volumes) and 25 corpus-wide (24 volumes) [M8, M9]; '\"asian mind\"' 7 / 13; scope share 35,214/312,169 = 1 in 8.86 ('about one document in nine'); decade densities of the regional part of C over dated non-apparatus regional documents: 1940s 165/9,577 = 17.2 per 1,000 (1 in 58), 1950s 382/12,112 = 31.5 (1 in 32), 1960s 397/7,884 = 50.4 (1 in 20), 1970s 104/3,370 = 30.9 (1 in 32), 1980s 1/106 [M10] — matching the overview's 'about one document in twenty' and the trace table's ~1 in 30 / ~1 in 60; '\"circular telegram 208\"' = 1 and '\"circular telegram\" AND 208' = 11 corpus-wide [§8]; 172 dropped / 166 bare USI; 121 files in raw/docs each with BODY length equal to length(body_text). Note: the memo's [M1] corpus-wide count (log line 19) is over all rows including apparatus; mine gives 0 either way.

STEP 3 (quotations): see fabricationDetails and miscitationDetails. The session's own checker (check_overview_quotes.py) was case-sensitive and substring-only over the 23 bodies; my check is the guide's segment-strict rule against the exact cited pair. 60 double-quoted spans in overview.md, no block quotes; 37 credited to documents + 29 excerpts = 66, all found; 23 non-document spans classified and checked as described.

STEP 4 (identifiers): 17 checked, 16 confirmed; see identifierDetails. Two further findings: the memo (§5 table) says lots 61D385, 63D224, 62D255, 60D322, 65F98, 62D181 and 55D339 get no row from lot-claimants or curated-lot-resolutions — lot-claimants has none of them, but curated-lot-resolutions.json does carry 62D181 ({kind: 'possible', seriesRef: 'conferenceFiles', displayName: 'Conference Files'}), so that sentence is wrong for one lot (not carried into the overview). frus1969-76v38p2/d105 is stored as RG 305 in document_sources exactly as the memo reports.

STEP 5 (deliverable): python3 -I check_collection.py collection.fruscollection frus-copy-2026-10-25.db -> '23 documents; all checks pass'. Entry counts by kind: heading 6, prose 6, document 23, excerpt 29, generated 1; all 23 documents carry a notes array; cited 23 / present 23 / missing none.

STEP 6 (vectors): see vectorUse. refuter/vectors_check.py decodes the index's segments independently (553/553 volumes round-trip, rows contiguous 0..314,615), reads sign bits at offset 64 of semantic-vectors-binary.bin (magic FRSV, ver 1, dims 512, docs 314,616; 340,560 trailing bytes = 660 x (512+4), the header's fourth word, centroids not documents), compares digests (index = binary@20 = map@20 = shard@16 = .generation = 89481b18…), reproduces the d31 neighbour list exactly (same ten pairs, same order, same Hamming 81/96/90/100/94/88/104/102/99/95, same raw and calibrated cosines after reranking the top-800 Hamming pool by int8 cosine from 168 shards), both baselines exactly (random pairs mean 167.1 sd 14.8 p1 132 min 95; 25th-neighbour median 107 q1 99 q3 114), the near-dup figures (d190–d185 32 bits, nearest of d190 is d185; d190–d207 50) and the cluster labels (138 cia/nsc/usia/inglis 2,189 docs; 29 lao/vietnamese/vietnam/thieu; 7 japanese/sato/japan/kishi; 31 indochina/minh/bao/dai).

STEP 7 (reach): refuter/archival_and_reach.py re-ran the logged document-returning queries: rank70 (log line 20) equals raw/rank_q1.txt exactly (70 rows); audience92 (line 22) equals raw/audience_ids.txt (92); the Japan query (line 24, LIMIT 20) returns d820, PubDipv06/d127 and v29p2/d46 among its 20; the core set (lines 26/28) as above; the circular-208 query (line 48) returns frus1950v07/d941 and frus1952-54v13p1/d116. Every one of the 23 cited documents is returned by at least one: 14 first by rank70, 6 first by audience92 (d551, d60, d992, v01/d26, v02/d29, v02/d197 — of which d551, d60 and d26 are NOT in C), 3 first by the Japan query, and d116 by the core set (line 26) and the circular query. Strict vector-reached 0, untraced 0, practical 0: d116, the only document the memo says a neighbour list surfaced (vectors.py, log line 40), was already in the saved raw/coreset.tsv (line 26) and raw/coreset_clean.tsv (line 28), so by the log's order it sat in a saved result set before the vector operation; the memo itself says it had not been read, which is consistent. V7 not applicable: the memo claims no vector-only document and that claim is confirmed.

STEP 8 (zeros): 11 listed; see zeros. Probe of the unqueried absence claim in overview §3 ('the Information Agency's opinion research and the country plans are summarized but not printed'): no scope document is headed as a country plan (FTS header:\"country plan\" = 0), but two USIA Research Service survey reports ARE printed in scope volume frus1917-72PubDipv08 — d34 (R-10-69, 'Effect of the Moon Landing on Opinions in Six Countries', Japan and the Philippines among them) and d94 (R-17-70, an eight-country survey including Japan on the Cambodia incursion) — so 'not printed' is contradicted for opinion research touching Asian audiences; the claim rests on no query in the memo or log.

STEP 9 (house figures): figures_check.txt lists 2 occurrences; reading the memo finds a third (line 170, 'I did not re-derive the one-in-sixty figure', spelled out). I verified the 1910-12-06 figure myself: SELECT MIN(d.date_iso) FROM external_citations e JOIN document_dates d … -> 1910-12-06 (true, but the session neither ran nor attributed it).

STEP 10 (dead terms): match_check lists 2 dead terms, both deliberate or noticed; 7 prefixes, 3 used without a vocab lookup of the stem (effect*, attitud*, intellectu*), none dead.

OTHER OBSERVATIONS: tally_run.md records the run at 12.5 min on claude-opus-5-5; the overview's 'Oriental mind' count relies on the FTS phrase (Porter-stemmed) and the memo's STRICT literal audit 14 of 14 (phrase_audit2.jsonl), which I did not re-read document by document; the overview's claim that C's documents are 'in the 81 … volumes' is the scope — C occupies 80 of them, as the memo says.
